correctness.rationale: For arbitrary m>=1, reconstruct the product coefficient as r_X(i)c_Y(j), sum over all blocks to isolate the row and column incidence profiles using positive integer constants 2 and m, and split into separated versus row-balanced cases. In the balanced case, constant column profiles force monochrome and paired even-size column types; balanced ranks force equipartitions. The exponential formula counts each uniquely, and explicit row/column permutation generators realize every block as a subgroup orbit. A standalone checker enumerated all Bell(2m) partitions for m=1..4, directly tested product closure, and matched the forms, totals 2,5,13,48, and automorphism orbits. m=5 formula 184 was evaluated but not exhaustively enumerated. No general theorem is inferred from the finite checks.

value.rationale: Rectangular bands are the first nontrivial direct-product family in the January 2026 semigroup Schur-ring program. The theorem gives a complete natural infinite-family classification, explicit subgroup-orbit realizations rather than merely counts, an exact EGF and quantified non-product examples (18 at \(m=4\)). The paper explicitly observes the lack of general classification beyond the direct-product construction; the new statement resolves that structural gap for one factor of size two. It is not solely a new small-case table or tautological restatement.
